# DC segmenting MD→wiki renderer module (pure capability; codec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Data Center stores rich text as wiki markup (REST v2), a lossy text format.
The `RichTextCodec` seam (epic e369, story J3) routes DC rich text through
`WikiTextCodec` (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:72`). `fit_outbound` (`:82`)
truncates strings above 32,767 characters with the established suffix;
`normalize_outbound` (`:96`) and `to_wire` (`:100`) pass strings through, while
`decode_inbound` (`:104`) passes strings through and maps `None` to empty. Thus DC
still ships rebar raw Markdown literally — `# Heading` reads as a hash.

Whole-body conversion is not an option: rebar prose is punctuation-dense and
pandoc's jira reader/writer mangles it. Verified on pandoc 3.6.1 in this
worktree: a prose `->` is escaped to `\->`; a Markdown table delimiter row comes
back as `| \-\-\- |`; punctuation inside inline code is escaped (`` `->` `` →
`{{\->}}`); and an HTML comment is **deleted outright** (a lone
`<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` renders to the empty string) — which would
drop rebar's own reconciler echo marker.

So the renderer **segments**: convert only structurally-safe units, pass
dangerous ones through verbatim.

**Why a pure module, not a codec change.** On DC the live outbound wire flows
THROUGH a codec op (`OutboundFieldMapper` composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(v))`;
the mapper is constructed with `WikiTextCodec` at `jira_datacenter/backend.py:89`).
So changing `to_wire`/`normalize_outbound` IS an immediate live cutover, and would
break the pinned identity tests (`test_rich_text_codec.py:244`, `:251`, `:183`) and
the codec law (`:163`). The cutover must land WITH echo-safety, which is story
3388's job. **This story ships only the pure renderer + tests and leaves every
`WikiTextCodec` operation unchanged, including `fit_outbound` truncation.** Nothing
observable changes on merge.

## Corpus fixture — RE-SCOPED (premise correction)
The original plan cited counts (179 code-arrow bodies, 70 erosion bodies,
68%/78% coverage) from a 2026-08-03 export. **That export no longer exists** — no
`parity_*.py`, no `parity-results.md`, no exported corpus, on disk or in git
history; rebar has no file-attachment store, so those `files/…` paths were an
ephemeral session workspace. The numbers are unreproducible and unauditable, so
they are replaced by numbers measured from a **committed** fixture.

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` enforces `check-added-large-files` at 500 KB/file, there
is no LFS, and `.gitignore` records a decision NOT to raise that cap — so the full
~5.9 MB body set cannot be vendored. The fixture is therefore a **stratified
sample** built by a committed generator, `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`
(deterministic seed; scrub-then-write, per `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py`
doctrine): every body exhibiting a phenomenon the renderer must be safe on, plus a
prose sample. Committed as `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/{code_arrow,table,prose}.json`
— 29 / 29 / 120 bodies, 178 total, each shard ≤127 KB.

## Approach
`adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` exposing `render_markdown_to_wiki(md) -> str`,
**not referenced by any codec op or live send path in this story**.

Split into blank-line blocks (fences kept whole) → classify each → render safe
units via the wheel-bundled pandoc (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`) → pass
dangerous units verbatim → reassemble preserving original order and spacing.

Four lossless rules, each forced by measured pandoc behavior:
- **Code-aware arrow substitution** (`-> <- <-> =>` → `→ ← ↔ ⇒`) on the Markdown
  BEFORE pandoc, skipping fenced/inline code. The HTML-comment delimiters `<!--`
  and `-->` are matched first and mapped to themselves, so `-->` is never rewritten
  to `-→`.
- **ASCII tables wrapped verbatim in `{noformat}`**, never converted.
- **HTML-comment and HTML/regex-dense blocks emitted verbatim** (pandoc deletes
  comments).
- **Post-render code-preservation check**: after converting a unit, every code
  fragment of the source must appear verbatim in the output; otherwise that unit
  falls back to its original Markdown. This turns pandoc's unpredictable escaping
  into a safe fallback instead of silent corruption.

A unit that already looks like wiki (`h1.`, `{code}`, `{{…}}`) is passed through,
so a Jira-authored body is never re-rendered as Markdown.

**pandoc delivery.** Pin `pypandoc-binary==1.15`, empirically confirmed here to
bundle pandoc 3.6.1, as a new `wiki` extra + in `dev` so CI exercises the exact
measured writer. Regenerate `uv.lock`; add `wiki:wiki` to the optional-extras
workflow so its real-wheel isolation lane and the existing EXTRAS parity test run.
If pandoc is absent or a unit fails, return input unchanged. The pure module is
unwired; timeout/process hardening remains in `ashy-waterlog-hamadryas` before
cutover.

`jira_family/` imports nothing from `adapters/jira/`
(`docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`), and pandoc is not a Cloud
dependency, so the renderer belongs here.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (new) — the segmenting renderer.
- `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py` (new) + `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` (new).
- `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` — `wiki` extra, dev pin, reproducible resolution;
  `src/rebar/_optional.py` — register it; `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` —
  exercise the extra in isolation and satisfy the EXTRAS parity guard.
- `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` — exclude the fixture (captured data, not
  authored text).
- **UNCHANGED:** `WikiTextCodec` and all its ops; `jira_datacenter/backend.py:154
  normalize_rich_text`; every live send site (all wired by 3388).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `render_markdown_to_wiki` renders safe units to wiki and passes dangerous
  units (tables, HTML-dense, regex-dense) verbatim, preserving order; verified by
  `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough`.
- [ ] Arrow substitution runs on the Markdown before pandoc and rewrites **zero**
  code arrows; verified by `test_dc_arrow_substitution_spares_code`.
- [ ] The HTML-comment terminator `-->` is never rewritten to `-→`; verified by
  `test_arrow_substitution_cases`.
- [ ] Over all 178 committed corpus bodies, **zero** arrow-bearing code fragments
  are lost; verified by `test_dc_corpus_no_code_arrow_is_ever_rewritten`.
- [ ] ASCII tables are wrapped verbatim in `{noformat}`, never converted; verified
  by `test_dc_table_noformat_stable`.
- [ ] All 31 corpus table bodies still contain a table after rendering; verified by
  `test_dc_corpus_tables_survive_verbatim`.
- [ ] Every HTML comment in the corpus survives rendering (pandoc deletes them);
  verified by `test_dc_corpus_html_comments_survive`.
- [ ] Rendering the same body on repeated passes is byte-identical; verified by
  `test_dc_corpus_render_is_deterministic_across_passes`.
- [ ] A body that is already wiki passes through unchanged; verified by
  `test_dc_already_wiki_body_passes_through`.
- [ ] When pandoc is unavailable `render_markdown_to_wiki` returns its input
  unchanged; verified by `test_dc_pandoc_absent_identity`.
- [ ] When a single unit fails to convert, that unit falls back to its original
  Markdown; verified by `test_dc_pandoc_failure_degrades_that_unit`.
- [ ] Corpus richness stays at or above ≥90% of bodies / ≥95% of characters
  (measured 92.7% / 98.4%); verified by `test_dc_corpus_coverage`.
- [ ] The committed fixture cardinality is pinned at 178 bodies; verified by
  `test_corpus_cardinality_is_pinned`.
- [ ] The committed fixture carries no unscrubbed emails, tenant hostnames or URLs;
  verified by `test_corpus_carries_no_unscrubbed_secrets`.
- [ ] `WikiTextCodec` stays identity and no live send site changes; verified by the
  existing `test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`,
  `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched` and the codec-law test staying
  green unmodified.
